title: Brianna
dek: A druid whose experience of repeated death shapes a difficult commitment to life, freedom and trial amid the Rahu war, and whose grief finds an outlet in useful service.

profile.personality: Brianna combines practical druidic problem-solving with a commitment to preserving personhood. Repeated death shapes her fear and judgment; withdrawal is part of her response, alongside argument, service and renewed connection.
profile.achievements: She adventures around Prima, survives the Rahu-war period, argues for a dangerous enemy to face trial, joins the Knights and asks Elenia to help restore Ghilsen. Wild Shape appearances as BearBri and BatBri belong to the same character.
profile.relationships: Ghilsen is her husband, with St. Anky officiating their marriage. Elenia moves from battlefield opponent to a source of recognition and restorative help. Magnus is an early companion whose later Rahu allegiance complicates that shared history.

body:
Brianna is a druid and adventurer who uses Wild Shape to solve practical problems and has repeatedly died and returned. During the Rahu war she argues that a dangerous enemy should live to face trial. Her marriage to Ghilsen, his freedom and his restoration are part of that history alongside her own expeditions and disputed decisions.

An adventurer in the danger

Early scenes show curiosity, movement and immediate physical problem-solving. BearBri and BatBri are Wild Shape identities of Brianna, rather than separate characters. The Dark Raven, despite sharing a player, remains a different adventurer.

She adventures in the same broad early-2025 period as Magnus, before their community is divided by the Rahu war. That prior companionship remains part of the history when his later allegiance turns him against former allies.

Trial and battlefield necessity

During the war, Brianna tries to preserve a dangerous Rahuvian combatant so that he can face trial. St. Anky later explains that intention. Elenia objects to the immediate danger of keeping him alive in an active battle and stops her.

Both concerns survive the later conversation: Brianna wants judgment rather than summary death, while Elenia fears further casualties. Compassion does not automatically settle battlefield method, and tactical disagreement does not erase the humanity of the person making the choice.

The memory of dying alone

In the supplied account of her conversation with Elenia, Brianna describes repeated deaths, including one only hours after her wedding. She remembers dying alone as the fighting continued and later fearing that the same experience was about to happen again. She describes sleeplessness, haunted dreams and persistent alarm. These are her reported experiences; the biography does not assign a medical diagnosis.

She initially resists having to explain her suffering before her choices can be understood. Elenia eventually apologizes and recognizes the care beneath Brianna’s decision while continuing to criticize its method. Their disagreement develops into listening and renewed connection.

Freedom, loss and restoration

St. Anky officiates Brianna and Ghilsen’s marriage. Ghilsen’s earlier enslavement makes freedom a personal obligation for Brianna: she wants the person she loves to retain agency and to return as himself.

After his death she preserves his body and joins the Knights in search of useful work when much of what she loves feels lost. At her request, Elenia invokes divine help through Mya and restores Ghilsen. His return changes their circumstances without erasing Brianna’s experience of losing him.

Re-entering responsibility

Brianna can withdraw when overwhelmed, but the recovered arc also shows her speaking, asking for help, entering service and continuing to adventure. A reasonable interpretation of these scenes is that grief seeks an outlet in usefulness, and that repeated death helps explain her insistence on preserving life. Neither interpretation makes every later choice inevitable.

The open record

Her earlier biography, exact wedding date, complete sequence and mechanics of her deaths, every perspective on the soldier incident, full Knights history and later life remain unresolved. Her account includes the costs of warfare and return alongside her marriage, druidic work and disputed decisions about preserving life.

The siege · a way over the wall

During the Rahu bombardment, Brianna says the destruction is falling on everyone, not only adventurers. When a house is hit, she hurries over to look for people who need help. The narrator establishes that the dangerous building is empty; no rescue from inside it follows.

She then proposes using transmutation to give the company cloudlike forms so they can cross the wall without damaging it. Asked how it works, she consults her notes and explains the time needed to change. She describes the spell as transport and concealment rather than a fighting form. The casting and her movement with the group are witnessed; her predictions about protection remain her explanation of the spell.

She follows the wall toward the bombardment and can locate the enemy engines. The war account follows what happens beyond this stage. Her contribution here is to find a way out while the town remains under fire.

Companions under pressure

The departure is strained. Aravil threatens Ghilsen and demands that Brianna control him, invoking the stakes of the war. Brianna tells him not to threaten her husband and says she does not want a fight, though she will do what she must. When he suggests restraint or magical enthrallment, she refuses his orders and again asks him to back off.

She continues preparing the cloud-form spell, asks who is coming and answers Sajhan’s concern about control over her own movement. The disagreement does not become a duel or an agreed command structure in this exchange. Brianna’s defense of Ghilsen and her practical help to the company occur together, without making the group harmonious or her every response patient.
